raw_case_text: A 28-year-old male from Santarem, Para, Brazil, with a history of leisure activities in a rural area, tractor driver, a known carrier of the HIV virus since 2010, however without previous follow-up, contacted us for the first time at Fundacao de Medicina Tropical Dr. Heitor Vieira Dourado, Manaus, Amazonas, Brazil, for investigation of left knee chronic monoarthritis associated with tegumentary lesions. He had been using zidovudine, lamivudine, lopinavir/ritonavir for three weeks, this being the first antiretroviral regimen used. He had never used prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. He denied being a smoker or alcohol user. He reported that the left knee arthritis appeared after local trauma identified five months before, preceding the tegumentary lesions that appeared two months after the fact. During the clinic exam, polymorphism of skin lesions was noted with pustules of follicular distribution, papules with central necrosis, erythematous-infiltrated plaques covered with pustules and ulcerated plaques, located on the face, trunk, abdomen and limbs, associated with left knee arthritis (Figures 1, 2 and 3A). Oral and genital mucosa were spared. Lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly were not observed. Blood cultures for aerobes, mycobacteria, fungi and leukocyte cream were negative. VDRL resulted non-reagent. The Leishmaniasis screening exam was negative. The analysis of synovial fluid suggested infectious arthritis. Left knee x-ray showed reduction of joint space and osteolytic patellar lesion (Figure 3B). Patient underwent surgical cleansing of joint, biopsy of synovial membrane and skin. Both exams identified round cells, birefringent, with multiple buddings compatible with P. brasiliensis (Figure 4). Culture of synovial tissue confirmed the finding. Complementary propedeutics suggested pulmonary involvement and the Xpert/MTB RIF  sputum test was negative. At the time of diagnosis T CD4+ count was 44 cells/mm3 . Patient was treated with Amphotericin B deoxycholate 50mg/day (cumulative dose of 650mg) but despite the therapy, his clinical condition worsened, progressing to death on the 20th day of hospitalization. Necropsy revealed involvement of lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenals and bone marrow, in addition to the previously described sites (Figure 5).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old HIV-positive male tractor driver from Santarem, Para, Brazil, presented with a 5-month history of chronic left knee monoarthritis and a 3-month history of disseminated polymorphic ulcerated and pustular skin lesions.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Five months before admission, following local trauma, the patient developed chronic left knee monoarthritis, followed 2 months later by widespread pustular, papulonecrotic, and ulcerated cutaneous plaques across his face, trunk, abdomen, and extremities. He had initiated antiretroviral therapy (zidovudine, lamivudine, and lopinavir/ritonavir) 3 weeks prior to presentation at the Tropical Medicine Foundation in Manaus.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection in 2010 without prior medical follow-up or Pneumocystis prophylaxis; tractor driver with rural leisure exposure in Santarem, Para, Brazil; denied smoking or alcohol use.
subjective.review_of_systems: Home medications: zidovudine, lamivudine, and lopinavir/ritonavir started 3 weeks prior; positive for left knee pain/swelling and disseminated skin lesions.

objective.physical_examination: Polymorphic cutaneous lesions across the face, trunk, abdomen, and extremities—including follicular pustules, papules with central necrosis, erythematous infiltrated plaques topped with pustules, and ulcerated plaques—accompanied by left knee monoarthritis; oral and genital mucosae were spared, and no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly was present.
objective.routine_investigations: Blood cultures for aerobes, mycobacteria, and fungi, buffy coat examination, VDRL, Leishmania screening, and sputum Xpert MTB/RIF were all negative. Left knee radiograph showed joint space narrowing and an osteolytic patellar lesion; synovial fluid analysis was consistent with infectious arthritis.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 44 cells/mm3. Surgical knee debridement with synovial membrane biopsy, synovial tissue culture, and skin biopsy all identified birefringent round yeast cells with multiple budding ('pilot's wheel' morphology) diagnostic of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Cutaneous/mucocutaneous leishmaniasis, tuberculosis, and syphilis were excluded; direct microscopy, histopathology, and culture of synovial tissue and skin biopsies confirmed disseminated juvenile/immunosuppressed-type paracoccidioidomycosis (Paracoccidioides brasiliensis) with osteoarticular (patellar/knee) and cutaneous involvement in a patient with advanced AIDS (CD4 44 cells/mm3). Despite surgical joint debridement and intravenous amphotericin B deoxycholate (50 mg/day, cumulative dose 650 mg), the patient deteriorated and died on hospital day 20, with autopsy confirming disseminated involvement of the lungs, liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenals, and bone marrow.
